chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Safwan, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abu al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) about the ʿAqīqah (sacrifice for the newborn), regarding the wealthy (al-mu'sir) and the poor (al-mu'sir), so he said: 'There is no obligation upon the one who does not find [the means].'

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: Aqiqah: The ritual sacrifice of an animal performed on behalf of a newborn child
key_terms.الْمُوسِرِ: Al-Mu'sir: The wealthy person who has sufficient means
key_terms.لَمْ يَجِدْ: Lam yajid: Did not find/have the capacity or means
key_terms.وَالْمُعْسِرِ: Wa al-Mu'sir: The poor person who has limited means

ai.seo_question: Is the Aqiqah sacrifice obligatory for everyone or only for the wealthy?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the ʿAqīqah is a recommended act (mustaḥabb) rather than a strict obligation (wājib), as the exemption for those who cannot afford it indicates the removal of burden (taklīf) based on financial capacity. This ruling aligns with the Shia scholarly consensus that distinguishes between the obligatory Ḍabḥ (slaughter) for vows and the voluntary nature of ʿAqīqah, emphasizing ease in religious practice for the common believer.
